sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Blank-Check Entity for Public Market Acquisition Mergers (SPAC)

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid Civil Law (Napoleonic code foundation) with EU-derived regulatory overlay and an Anglo-American-inspired partnership vehicle (SCSp, modeled on the Delaware LP / UK LP under the Law of 23 July 2016)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States DTA (2002, as amended by the 2019 Protocol) – active
Luxembourg–China DTA (1994, as amended by the 1995 exchange of notes) – active
Luxembourg–United Kingdom DTA (1967, as amended) – active
BLEU (Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union) BIT network – active for non-EU counterparties; intra-EU BITs terminated post-Achmea (CJEU C-284/16)
EU-level FTAs and EPAs extended to Luxembourg (e.g., EU–Singapore, EU–South Korea, EU–Japan EPA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (AML Law), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 (AMLD5 transposition) and further amended by the Law of 25 July 2023; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2010 on identification of beneficial owners; CSSF Circular 24/850 (consolidated AML/CFT rules); Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, art. 738-1 et seq. (SCSp).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (with legitimate-interest access): following the CJEU judgment in C-37/20 (22 November 2022), public access to the Luxembourg RBE register is withdrawn; access is limited to (i) Luxembourg competent authorities, (ii) AML/CFT obliged entities, and (iii) persons demonstrating a legitimate interest.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing (extrait de registre) of each corporate limited partner and the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry or trade registry (e.g., UK Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations, Netherlands Chamber of Commerce)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for all Apostille Convention contracting states; otherwise Consular Legalization at the Luxembourg Embassy or consular post in the origin country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney of each partner-signatory (notarized) authorizing execution of the SCSp limited partnership agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the partner's domicile jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the notarial certificate; Consular Legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies (or EU national identity cards) of all ultimate beneficial owners and natural-person limited partners, together with proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or passport-issuing authority in the origin jurisdiction (certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the notarial certification; Consular Legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and AML clearance letter for each partner covering source of funds, banking relationship standing, and reputational integrity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank or private bank of the partner (letter notarized by the issuing bank's notary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the notarial attestation; Consular Legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of wealth / source of funds declaration and organizational chart for UBO piercing, including all intermediate holding entities above the 25% threshold
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the origin jurisdiction (certified declaration) and authorized corporate service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the notarial deed; Consular Legalization for non-Hague states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, general partners, directors, authorized signatories and trusted intermediaries against: (i) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (ii) EU restrictive measures (FISMA/EEAS consolidated financial sanctions database); (iii) OFAC SDN list (adopted as best-practice internal policy, not a Luxembourg statutory mandate); (iv) FATF high-risk and monitored jurisdictions lists; and (v) national Luxembourg alerts issued by the Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF). PEP status triggers enhanced due diligence (EDD) under Article 3(7) of the AML Law; enhanced scrutiny is equally applied to SPAC special purpose vehicles, escrow counterparties, and trust-account beneficiaries. Screening results are documented, GDPR-aligned, and retained for a minimum of five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – www.lbr.lu (delegate operator of the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS); name clearance executed via the electronic 'Nom et forme' reservation module with Luxtrust or EU eID authentication
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory filings and the corporate name must be submitted in Luxembourgish, French or German; where the trade name originates in non-Latin script (e.g., CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic), a mandatory Latin-script transliteration is required and the transliterated form is the registered name. The legal-form suffix 'Société en commandite spéciale' or 'SCSp' must appear on all corporate documents (Article 738-1, Law of 10 August 1915).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Établissement de crédit (prior CSSF authorization required)
Assurance / Réassurance / Assureur (prior CSSF authorization required)
SICAV / FCP / Fonds d'investissement / OPCVM / AIF (prior CSSF authorization under EU AIFMD / UCITS regimes)
Bourse / Exchange / Négociateur / Market Operator (prior CSSF and Ministry of the Economy authorization required)
État du Luxembourg / Grand-Duché / Luxembourg (misleading reference to the State — approval by the Ministry of Justice required)
Société Nationale / Chambre de Commerce / Chambre des Métiers (reserved names of public bodies)
SPAC / Blank-Check / Special Purpose Acquisition (use permitted only with accurate 'SCSp' legal-form suffix; no prior approval required)
Avocat / Notaire / Expert-Comptable / Réviseur d'entreprises (protected titles of regulated professions)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No statutory extension: upon expiry of the 60-day reservation window the applicant must file a fresh name-reservation request and re-pay the EUR 22.50 fee, provided the name remains available on the RCS index. In case of refusal, the RCS/LBR issues a reasoned notice; the applicant may (i) re-file a corrected name within the same session, or (ii) lodge a formal administrative appeal (recours en annulation) with the Tribunal administratif in Luxembourg City within three months of notification, pursuant to the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS. Market practice is to submit an iterative re-filing with the correcting legal-entity token plus a memorandum addressing the refusal grounds.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for this SPAC-class SCSp: a fixed registered office in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg is mandatory under Article 738-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915. Where a domiciliation agent is used, the agent must hold a license under the Law of 31 May 1999 on domiciliation agents. For any listing-bound SPAC, Euronext Luxembourg, the CSSF and market practice require substantive physical office presence with accessible statutory records, minute books, and regulatory filings; pure virtual or mail-forwarding arrangements are non-compliant.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: ≈20% at pre-incorporation stage (notarial verification, bank source-of-funds inspection, UBO documentation review by the RBE and the CRF); rising to ≈60–75% after admission to trading or upon CSSF licensing, where unannounced inspections are authorized under Article 8 of the AML Law and CSSF Regulation 12-02.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Electronic name clearance and reservation fee (RCS via LBR portal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 March 2018; EUR 22.50 per reservation application

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed for the SCSp limited partnership agreement (authentic form, institutional SPAC standard)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary – Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff plus drafting component proportionate to complexity and capital scale of the SCSp; market range EUR 2,000–3,500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS tariff, EUR 70 for electronic transmission with full annexes

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RESA – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (via LBR)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff, EUR 40–70 depending on page volume

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register (RBE) declaration and UBO piercing analysis for the SCSp
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RBE – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (LBR); professional fee payable to the conducting law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: State filing is free of charge; market professional fee of EUR 350 for multi-layer ownership chart, control verification, and RBE submission

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT automated screening: PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, FATF and CRF watchlist checks
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: CSSF-licensed KYC database vendor (e.g., World-Check, Dow Jones); plus Luxembourg counsel administrative fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per-subject annual screening license and investigation fee, EUR 1,000 for 5–8 subjects

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization of foreign corporate document bundle (approximately 5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Origin-country apostille authorities; Luxembourg Embassy or consular posts in non-Hague states
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Origin-state tariffs vary, EUR 70–200 per document; weighted average USD 165 x 5 documents, plus courier and translation tolerances

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Stage-1 legal and tax counsel fees (pre-incorporation due diligence, name clearance, suitability review, LPA drafting instructions)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm (ELS) and tax advisor (ELTA member)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark EUR 8,000–15,000 for SPAC-class SCSp formation and regulatory suitability review

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Arts. 944-1 to 944-20 (SCSp regime inserted by the Law of 23 July 2016); supplemented by the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers and the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg City
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif / partnership agreement (contrat de société) accompanied by the declaration of the general partner, registered with the RCS and published in the RESA
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital or paid-up capital requirement for an SCSp (Art. 944-2 of the Law of 10 August 1915, as amended); partners freely determine subscription instalments in the partnership agreement. For a SPAC, the offering proceeds must be segregated in a trust/escrow account held with a Luxembourg credit institution until a Business Combination, liquidation or redemption event; no statutory capital escrow deposit is otherwise required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company, a Luxembourg société en commandite spéciale, be incorporated under the Law of 10 August 1915, as amended; the annexed partnership agreement be approved; the subscriptions of Partnership Interests by the Initial Partners be accepted; the registered office be fixed at [address], Luxembourg; [Name] be appointed General Partner and Manager with full powers to bind the Company; the General Partner is instructed to file the formation deed with the Luxembourg Business Registers, to effect RESA publication, and to open bank, trust and escrow accounts; and any act necessary for the incorporation, listing preparation and the initial Business Combination is authorised.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability reservation and registered office validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) e-Desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name-reservation request via the RCS e-Desk portal for the proposed SCSp name, which must include the suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'; provide the intended registered office address in Luxembourg City and, if required, the landlord's occupancy consent. The RCS validates the name against the register and public-policy constraints of the Law of 10 August 1915. Preserve the reservation certificate for submission with the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name with SCSp suffix
Passport copy of the general partner or authorised representative
Landlord / head-lease consent for the registered office address
RCS name-reservation form (RCS 1A)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to conflict or public-policy grounds, file an amended name list or submit a priority explanation to the RCS registrar; the objection is curable within 5 business days by submitting three alternative names in preferential order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the partnership agreement and initial subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public registered with the Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement (contrat de société) in English or French and execute it, preferably as a notarial deed (acte notarié) to facilitate bank, exchange and counterparty recognition. The notary verifies identity, capacity, the non-conviction declaration and the powers of the general partner, and records the initial subscription of Partnership Interests. The deed must incorporate the mandatory SCSp provisions of Arts. 944-1 to 944-20, including limited liability of the special partners and unlimited liability of the general partner, and must set out the SPAC escrow mechanics if applicable.
required_dossiers: Valid passport / national ID of the general partner and special partners
Certificate of residence or tax identification of the partners
AML/KYC forms and source-of-funds statements
RCS name-reservation certificate from Step 1
Bank reference letter for the partners
Declaration de non-condamnation (no prior conviction) of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries AML/KYC documentation, supply supplementary source-of-funds evidence and a beneficial-ownership chart within 10 business days; if the deed is rejected for drafting deficiencies, execute a corrective addendum (avenant) and re-notarise the amended agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and RESA legal publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS registration department, Luxembourg City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial deed and the accompanying RCS award form, together with the appointment of the general partner and the registered-office declaration, online via the RCS portal or at the RCS counter. The registry then issues the RCS extract (extrait du RCS) with the Luxembourg registration number (numéro d'immatriculation) and arranges publication in the RESA. Pay the statutory registration fee upon submission.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed of partnership agreement
RCS filing form (F1 or applicable module)
Copy of the first resolution appointing the general partner
Proof of the general partner's appointment and capacity
Declaration of the registered office address
Payment confirmation of the RCS registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a formal query, respond within the 30-day statutory deadline with corrected data; if registration is suspended for incomplete annexes, re-submit the missing documents and request a new priority date; late payment penalties may be cured by immediate settlement and a written explanation to the LBR.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED); Luxembourg Business Registers for the beneficial-ownership register (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp with the ACD for income tax and municipal business tax (impôt commercial) using the RCS-generated identification data; file the partner information and, if applicable, the elective tax-transparency confirmation. If the SPAC will receive VAT-able services, file the AED registration form (CV-301) to obtain a VAT number. Separately, file the beneficial-ownership declaration with the RBE within one month of registration. The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default for direct taxes.
required_dossiers: RCS extract dated within three months
Certified copy of the partnership agreement
Partner register / beneficial-ownership filing (RBE)
ACD identification forms (Form 1002 / 1003)
Bank confirmation of the SCSp's IBAN for potential VAT refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ACD contests the transparent characterisation, file a formal objection (réclamation préalable) with the partnership tax desk of the ACD; if the AED rejects the VAT application, supplement the information and re-file within 5 business days of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of SPAC trust/escrow account and listing-readiness confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (CSSF-supervised) and Luxembourg Stock Exchange (LuxSE) listings team
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarial deed, RCS extract and the first corporate resolutions to the bank's account-opening committee; execute the account mandates for the SPAC trust/escrow account, ensuring compliance with CSSF AML/KYC circulars and arrival of Swift wires. The escrow instructions must ring-fence the offering proceeds and permit release only upon the conditions of the Business Combination, redemption or liquidation, as defined in the partnership agreement. Thereafter, coordinate with the LuxSE listings team for admission-to-listing preparation.
required_dossiers: Certified RCS extract
Notarial partnership agreement and first corporate resolutions
AML/KYC identification of the general partner, special partners and source of funds
SPAC business rationale and financial projections
Escrow agreement or trust deed in a form acceptable to the Luxembourg bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced KYC due diligence under the Medium-Risk-Enhanced AML tier, provide a sponsor-profile memorandum and a full beneficial-ownership chart within 10 business days; if the escrow structure is contested, renegotiate the trust deed and submit the revised version to the bank's legal division for approval.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie — Direction générale de l'industrie et de la compétitivité (general establishment permit, if any physical premise is used); for SPAC financial-market access: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and Luxembourg Stock Exchange (LuxSE) admission board
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: CSSF visa on the SPAC prospectus under the Luxembourg Law of 16 July 2019 on prospectuses for securities, and LuxSE admission-to-listing confirmation for the Official List / Euro MTF; supplemented by the general business-establishment attestation, where applicable

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement — Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no industrial installation; the SCSp is an office-based financial vehicle without pollution-generating facilities. A Class 4 Notification only applies if a human-occupied workplace exceeding the communal zoning thresholds is established; no full EIA Report is required under the Law of 22 May 2008 on environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No regulated process wastewater or VOC emissions arise from office operations; municipal wastewater discharges comply with EU Directive 91/271/EEC via the communal sanitation network; waste handling follows the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management with e-waste (WEEE) routed per Directive 2012/19/EU; any refrigeration equipment must use working fluids compliant with Regulation (EU) No 517/2014.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: CGDIS fire-safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) confirming means of egress, smoke detection and fire extinguishers; structural load / building-occupancy attestation for the leased registered office; occupational-safety clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM); and, where staff are employed, registration with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and indirect taxes. Central business registration is conducted via the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) with electronic filing through MyGuichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing an SCSp must first appoint a Luxembourg-licensed authorized representative/agent. The constitutive dossier is filed with the RCS, and upon incorporation the entity receives a commercial registration number (matricule) which functions as the national tax identification number (TIN). If taxable activities for VAT purposes are present, a separate VAT identification number is requested from the AEDT using Form 511, accompanied by identity documentation, proof of RCS registration, and details of the appointed VAT representative when the entity is non-resident. For direct tax purposes, the SCSp must file a registration declaration (Formulaire 64) with the ACD unless wholly tax-transparent and not subject to Luxembourg taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An SCSp is fiscally transparent by default, but may irrevocably elect to be treated as a taxable corporate entity under Article 175bis of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR) through a formal declaration to the ACD. Additionally, hybrid mismatch elections and alignment statements under EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) rules can be filed to coordinate the entity's treatment with foreign jurisdictions where investors are established, preventing double taxation or double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies; VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction in Luxembourg. A simplified small-business franchise regime is available for taxable annual turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000, but this does not exempt the entity from registration if it engages in significant intra-EU acquisitions or imports subject to reverse charge.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose mandatory real-time e-invoicing or digital fiscal clearance. Electronic invoicing is accepted under the same conditions as paper invoices. B2B e-invoicing is optional, but recapitulative statements (EC Sales Lists) must be filed electronically for intra-Community supplies. The tax administration is preparing for the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) framework; no digital stamping or API clearance system is operational to date.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods dispatched or transported by the seller or on his behalf to a destination outside the European Union, provided the goods are physically exported, a valid export declaration is accepted by the Luxembourg customs authorities, and documentary proof of export is retained. Services physically realized abroad and services directly related to import/export operations may also be zero-rated. An SCSp typically engages in exempt financial services and share-dealing activities, which are outside the scope of VAT rather than zero-rated; any related export servicing must satisfy the same evidence requirements to claim 0%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading / CMR waybill / Air Waybill
Proof of dispatch and leaving the EU territory
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent claims of export zero-rating or misrepresentation of export documents are subject to a 50% fine of the evaded VAT under Article 62 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, plus late-payment interest at 0.8% per month. In egregious cases, criminal sanctions may include imprisonment. Input VAT recoverable on exports is clawed back retroactively if the required export proofs are not produced within the prescribed statutory period (10 years), with interest running from the original claim date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) as the national central bank subsidiary of the Eurosystem; the European Central Bank (ECB) exercises Eurozone monetary policy authority. Financial-sector supervision is managed by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), which also enforces cash-control declarations and AML/CFT obligations. No separate Luxembourg foreign-exchange administration exists; capital-flow statistics and FX data are reported to BCL for balance-of-payments purposes only.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies a fully liberalised capital and current-account regime pursuant to Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). The euro is unconditionally convertible; no exchange-control approval, hard-currency surrender rule, or central-bank licensing is required for SPAC capital contributions, IPO escrow deposits, acquisition disbursements, or partner distributions. The principal remittance hurdles are indirect: CSSF AML/CFT due diligence under the amended Law of 12 November 2004, sanction screening under EU Regulation 269/2014 and national freezing measures, CRS/FATCA reporting, and UBO registration under the Luxembourg RBE law. A tax-transparent SCSp operates with no entity-level withholding on interest or dividends; partners are taxed on their allocated income, and profit repatriation to non-resident partners is unrestricted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory repatriation timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation on export receipts, foreign currency revenues, or inbound investment proceeds. A Luxembourg SCSp may maintain multi-currency accounts (USD, EUR, GBP, CHF) without restriction. The only applicable obligation is physical cash transport declaration for amounts exceeding EUR 10,000 under Regulation (EU) 2018/1672, administered by Luxembourg customs, and prudent treasury reporting to the BCL for statistical Purposes when cross-border payments are made.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low-to-Medium for operating expenses; unacceptable for IPO equity or redemption escrow custody. Luxembourg-licensed e-money institutions (EMIs) and EEA passporting EMIs supervised by the CSSF can open multi-currency current accounts with SEPA and SWIFT MT103 issuance, but they may not hold trust-grade escrow client funds within the meaning of the Luxembourg law of 18 December 2009 on payment services, nor can they provide the custodian/trustee-grade chain required by a SPAC listing prospectus. Offshore non-EEA digital EMIs are legally prohibited from providing treasury services to a Luxembourg-domiciled SCSp without an EU banking licence or EMI passport; any attempt to route subscription proceeds through such platforms will trigger automatic AML rejection and potential CSSF enforcement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No absolute statutory mandate exists under Luxembourg law for physical presence of directors or the general partner (GP). Remote onboarding is permissible under a risk-based CSSF AML approach, typically via a compliant video interview with two authorised compliance officers, certified passport pages, and notarised apostilled entity documents. In practice, BIL, Banque de Luxembourg, and BNP Paribas Luxembourg accept fully remote opening where the GP and all material UBOs are established in EU- or FATF-equivalent jurisdictions. For SPAC sponsor vehicles with non-EU or sanctions-sensitive shareholders, at least one physical, notarised identification ceremony at the bank's Luxembourg head office is frequently required, and the GP must evidence economic substance (registered office, resident director, administrative infrastructure) under Article 159 of the Luxembourg company law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SPAC sponsor structure containing orphan entities, nominee shareholders, or layered holding partnerships that obscure the ultimate beneficial owner chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete Luxembourg RBE extract showing no inconsistencies; signed SCSp limited partnership agreement (LPA) with all annexes and side letters; group structure chart referencing the sponsor's parent entity; full-chain UBO declaration; legal opinion from an admitted Luxembourg avocat confirming the UBO filiation and absence of bearer shares or opacification arrangements

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large IPO escrow deposits from third-party institutional sponsors and placement agent wires exceeding standard due-diligence thresholds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements for each contributing sponsor entity; signed underwriting and escrow agreements; sponsor's committed capital letter showing explicit source of funds (realised proceeds of prior funds, audited financials, or verified liquid assets); complete SWIFT MT103/MT202 history of each wire; independent auditor comfort letter confirming escrow custody; declarations against investor brokering or non-compliance with SEC SPAC rules where applicable

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse-media or sanctions/PEP flags arising from placement agents, promoters, or sub-custodians involved in the SPAC listing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time sanctions screening results against consolidated EU lists, OFAC SDN, and UN Security Council lists including jurisdiction-geolocation evidence; PEP genealogy map for every person holding 10% or more of units and all executive officers; compliance assurance letters from each introducing broker; negative-news and adverse-media search reports dated within 90 calendar days of onboarding; remedial disclosure and written no-objection correspondence from the bank's AML committee

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Classification risk of the SCSp as an unregulated alternative investment fund (AIF), triggering AIFMD licensing, MiFID promotion restrictions, or unauthorised public distribution concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CSSF written confirmation or reasoned legal opinion that the SCSp operates as a SPAC holding vehicle outside AIFMD authorisation or with an authorised registered AIFM; CSSF prospectus visa where units are publicly offered; AIFMD exemption assessment under Article 2 or Article 4(1)(i); UCITS road-show analysis; Luxembourg tax certificate confirming pass-through treatment and absence of licence-to-lend or deposit-taking activity

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Recommended protocol: SWIFT MT103 (for direct third-party sponsor transfers) or SEPA Credit Transfer (for EUR contributions up to EUR 100,000) to the SCSp operational account, using transaction purpose code identifying a capital contribution under the partnership agreement. For USD-denominated escrow injections, route via correspondent clearing using SWIFT MT103/MT202COV to the bank's US correspondent (e.g., BIL's New York clearing agent), quoting the SCSp's account number and reference 'SCSp capital contribution to SPAC escrow'. All wires must be accompanied by a board-resolution extract and, where required by the receiving bank, a scanned capital contribution schedule signed by the general partner. Inbound payments should not be split; any single wire above EUR/USD 50,000 triggers automatic enhanced due-diligence review. BCL statistical reporting applies only for balance-of-payments aggregation, not approval; no central-bank permit is required. For cash deliveries, Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 declaration applies above EUR 10,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail for target-company merger consideration and redemption payments is SWIFT MT103, issued upon authenticated instructions from the GP with dual approval conditioned on the corporate approval framework (CAF) limits. High-value simultaneous settlements and interbank flows require SWIFT MT202/MT202COV cover payments via correspondent banks. For trade-related operational disbursements, commercial letters of credit under ICC UCP 600 issued by the banking desk are permitted, with all presentation and compliance documents maturing in the escrow's trusted network. Domestic and EU euro payments may clear via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) up to EUR 100,000 per transaction without additional controls. On completion of a de-SPAC merger, the transfer agent executes DTC settlement in the United States and synchronises with Clearstream Banking Luxembourg or Euroclear for any cross-listed units; simultaneous SWIFT MT199 internal transfers between the escrow and operational accounts require the trustee or depositary's counter-signature.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD deliverable forwards with maturity aligned to SPAC life-cycle drawdowns (typically 12 to 24 months), executed with CRD IV-licensed counterparty banks

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing emerging-market restricted currencies where the target company's business is exposed (e.g., USD/RMB, USD/IDR, USD/BRL), subject to CSSF risk-upgrade notification and internal capital adequacy treatment under CRR
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps converting USD sponsor loans to EUR fixed-rate liabilities, cleared or bilateral with mandatory EMIR trade reporting to an approved trade repository
Plain vanilla FX options and zero-premium collar structures for corridor-protecting USD/EUR conversion proceeds from IPO escrow interest and potential target-company pay-outs
Short-dated FX spot contracts only for operational expense EUR/USD conversions, with settlement via CLS or continuous linked settlement bank counterparties where available

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of RCS Registration Data (Confirmation annuelle des données au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) via eRCS online filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 31 March of each calendar year in accordance with the RCS annual confirmation cycle; exact dates follow the Luxembourg Business Registers e-Confirmation schedule for the current year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative warning, coercive monetary penalty (astreinte) enforceable by the RCS, potential judicial strike-off (radiation) from the commercial register after repeated non-compliance, and consequential loss of corporate capacity to enter into binding transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Re-Confirmation / Update Declaration (RBE — Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in the ownership or control structure of the SCSp; in the absence of changes, annual accuracy review must be performed during the RCS annual confirmation window (1 January to 31 March)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report a UBO change within 30 days exposes the SCSp and its General Partner to criminal fines from EUR 500 to EUR 1,250; knowingly false or incomplete declarations may attract fines up to EUR 5,000, imprisonment in serious cases, and administrative de-registration consequences.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Transparent Partnership Income Tax Return (Form 100 / partnership income allocation declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 December of the year following the relevant fiscal year for electronic filing via MyGuichet/ACD portal; 31 May direct filing window if paper filing applies; extensions are available only upon formal request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing assessment (taxation d'office), administrative fines under direct tax procedure, statutory late-payment interest accrued at 0.5% per month, and payment enforcement measures including seizure of partner distributions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Value Added Tax Return (Déclaration TVA annuelle), applicable only where the SCSp is a VAT taxable person
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 January following the close of the calendar year for annual VAT declarants; monthly or quarterly VAT returns may apply depending on the turnover threshold; no VAT return is required where the SCSp has no taxable economic activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to EUR 750 per return, late-payment interest at 0.6% per month according to VAT collection rules, and enforced debt collection procedure by the tax authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts and Statutory Audit Report Deposit (only applicable if the SCSp qualifies as a large undertaking or regulated public-interest entity; standard SCSp is exempt from public accounts filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not required for a standard fiscally-transparent SCSp; if the audit threshold or a regulatory classification applies, annual accounts must be prepared under Luxembourg GAAP and deposited within eight months of the balance sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Compulsory deposit order, administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 in case of non-publication, personal liability exposure of the General Partner, and possible commercial court strike-off proceedings for persistent default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SCSp is subject to mandatory independent statutory audit if it constitutes an undertaking within the meaning of the 2016 Luxembourg audit law and exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total exceeding EUR 20,000,000, net turnover exceeding EUR 40,000,000, or average payroll exceeding 250 employees. A public-interest entity status, such as a SPAC listed or pre-listed on a Luxembourg or EU regulated market, triggers compulsory audit irrespective of size. Certain regulated activities, including alternative investment fund management or custody arrangements, may impose audit requirements based on the applicable sectoral law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as derived from the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial register and annual accounts, as amended, and the accompanying accounting regulations; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for consolidated financial statements of Luxembourg listed groups and, under defined conditions, for individual accounts. A standard transparent SCSp maintains internal books and records under Luxembourg GAAP but is not ordinarily required to publish statutory financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Luxembourg law of 13 January 2019 on the register of beneficial owners, the SCSp must file initial UBO data with the RBE and update such data within 30 days of any change in ownership, control, or economic rights. As a routine annual compliance measure, the General Partner must formally re-confirm the identity, nationality, and economic interest percentage of each beneficial owner during the annual RCS confirmation window. An annual external re-filing is not separately invoiced by the RBE where no data has changed, but the internal confirmation record must be documented and retained.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (Assignments and Purchases of Partnership Interests and Capital Accounts)
Register of General Partner Appointments, Conducting Manager Mandates and Their Revocations
Minute Book of Partner Meetings and General Partner Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – 3,500 per year for registered office, resident registered agent, and annual corporate secretarial filing services in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 25,000 – 60,000 per audit for a small-to-mid-size SPAC/SCSp structure in Luxembourg; higher for consolidated, regulated, or publicly-traded vehicles
